claims.statement: ExecutionEngine.executeTask enforces a fixed preflight governance order: in-memory/durable duplicate and running-state guards (durable RUNNING throws TASK_RUNNING), execution_recovery_hold and deep_agent_assurance_hold metadata checks (throwing EXECUTION_RECOVERY_REQUIRED / DEEP_AGENT_ASSURANCE_HOLD), a pending execution-only approval check, a runtime-governance isAllowed check that cancels the task when the assigned agent is quarantined or circuit-breaker-tripped, loop-pause / agent-availability / skill-attribution asserts (LOOP_OPERATOR_PAUSED, AGENT_UNAVAILABLE, denied), an observed-version runtime admission gate (admitRuntime, shadow mode logs but does not enforce), and only then CommandRiskClassifier.assessTask, PolicyDecisionService.evaluate, and GovernanceGateService tightening before the task is queued.

CommandRiskClassifier screens commands against ordered regex tiers (critical patterns and outside-workspace writes recommend deny; high and medium mutation patterns recommend require_approval; read-only patterns recommend allow) and is fail-closed: an unrecognized command defaults to MEDIUM risk with require_approval, never allow.

CommandRiskClassifier.assessTask elevates risk for sensitive keywords and local opencode execution, treats review_only tasks as low risk, defers to classify() when task.metadata.requested_command is present, and forces recommended_decision to deny whenever the resulting risk level is CRITICAL.

PolicyDecisionService.evaluate loads enabled approval_policies ordered by priority DESC then created_at DESC, applies the first matching policy, compiles policy match_pattern through ReDoSGuard (dangerous or invalid patterns never match), overrides to deny when the tool is in the policy's blocked_tools, and falls back to the classifier's recommended_decision when no policy matches.

GovernanceGateService is default-off (GOVERNANCE_GATE_ENABLED=true arms it), looks up OpenMythos benchmark evidence by task agent_id then nightly:<model> from GOVERNANCE_GATE_MODEL_MAP then metadata subject_model, returns allow when no evidence exists, and when the latest score is below the floor returns require_approval with a trend and optionally flagRetirement after three consecutive below-floor declining runs — it only ever tightens allow to require_approval and never loosens a deny or approval outcome.

GOVERNANCE_GATE_FLOOR defaults to 3, calibrated for a 0-5 score scale while observed openmythos_eval_runs.overall_score values range roughly 0-95, and floor() accepts any finite non-negative value (a former <=5 clamp was removed), so operators must set the floor explicitly when arming the gate or it only catches near-zero runs.

ToolBroker.evaluateToolCall rate-limits per principal (100 requests per 60s sliding window plus 10-per-second burst, throwing RateLimitExceeded), defaults to deny for unknown tools, escalates allow to require_approval at or above require_approval_above_risk (default HIGH), blocks self-allow after more than 5 allow decisions by the same principal on a task within one hour (separation of duties), and persists every decision with an immutable dec-<uuid> decision id in tool_broker_decisions.

ToolBroker capability tokens issued on allow are durable rows in tool_broker_capability_tokens scoped to category:tool, task, and principal with a 900-second default TTL; validateCapabilityToken requires tool, task, and presenting principal to all match and deletes expired tokens, and reevaluateOnParameterChange deletes the original token and re-runs the full evaluation when parameters change.

CLI executors do not mediate their internal tools through ToolBroker, so constructing a broker in ExecutionEngine does not enforce per-tool policy; callers must call evaluateToolCall before execution and validateCapabilityToken at the effect boundary themselves.

ApprovalService.createApproval stamps expires_at with approvalTtlMs() (APPROVAL_TTL_MS, default 1 hour, clamped to 5 min .. 7 days) and writes the approval row, its required djimitflo.approval.requested outbox event (enqueueRequiredEvent, inside the same transaction), and the canonical APPROVAL_REQUESTED audit entry in a single immediate transaction, so a failed audit or outbox insert rolls the approval back; the WebSocket broadcast, best-effort Telegram pushApproval, and post-commit recordDecision (authority-ledger) happen only after commit, and a broadcast failure is logged but never undoes the decision.

ApprovalService.decideApproval runs in an immediate transaction, rejects decisions on expired approvals (persisting expiry and its audit inside the transaction, committing, then throwing APPROVAL_EXPIRED), enforces self-approval prevention at the data layer by throwing SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN when decidedBy equals requested_by, and refuses to process a non-pending approval twice.

Approval expiry is realized lazily on read or on a decision attempt, and realize-expiry cancels a task still in awaiting_approval (guarded so tasks that moved on are untouched) with its own task_cancelled_after_approval_expiry audit row, mirroring what a denial does.

Manual-action approvals (metadata.manual_action: true, created via POST /api/approvals) never gate or resume execution: getLatestPendingForTask with executionOnly filters them via a json_type(metadata, '$.manual_action') != 'true' predicate before LIMIT so a newer manual review cannot hide an older execution gate, and handleApprovalDecision records their decisions as evidence and returns without dispatching.

Each approval lifecycle step is mirrored best-effort (never blocking the approval) to the append-only authority_events ledger with a sha-256 payload digest and per-correlation sequence, and emits djimitflo.approval.requested/approved/denied/expired domain events into event_outbox; the approval events use the required producer class whose insert is atomic with the state change, while EVENT_PUBLISH_ENABLED=true is still required for the row to be written and for EventOutboxService to drain pending rows to the external DJIMIT_EVENT_BUS_URL.

ExecutionEngine.hasApprovedStart treats an approval as a valid execution grant only if it matches the executor kind, is not a manual action, has not expired, and its stored executionInputHash equals a fresh sha-256 hash of the task's dispatch-relevant fields; when that direct check fails it may still return true via the opt-in reviewerInheritsRunApproval escape, so a stale or edited grant otherwise forces a new approval before dispatch.

executeTask revalidates admission after the runtimeConcurrencySemaphore capacity wait: the execution input hash must be unchanged and the loop-pause, agent-availability, recovery-hold, risk classification, policy evaluation, and gate assessment checks run again, with a tightened outcome aborting via EXECUTION_POLICY_DENIED or EXECUTION_APPROVAL_STALE rather than dispatching on stale authority; a granted approval resumes by re-entering executeTask.

AuditService is a façade over ComplianceAuditService: record() maps AuditEventCreateInput to appendEntry, deriving outcome from the event type (denied/violation to denied, failed/error to failure, else success) and defaulting actor to system, while both read and write the same audit_events table.

ComplianceAuditService.appendEntry hash-chains every audit_events row: previousHash is the latest entry's hash (or 'genesis'), hash is sha-256 over canonical JSON with deeply sorted keys, chain_sequence is MAX+1, SQLite triggers on audit_events and the compliance_audit_log view raise errors on UPDATE/DELETE making the log append-only, and verifyChain replays the chain checking linkage and recomputed hashes.

ApprovalService.createApproval merges loopApprovalLink() into the approval metadata before caller metadata overrides: it reads the worker task's metadata.loop_run_id/lease_id and joins loop_runs to goals to record loop_run_id, lease_id, goal_id and improvement_id on the approval at creation, so the approval to goal to outcome join no longer depends on the task row; the helper is empty for non-loop tasks and fail-soft.

ApprovalService.recordDecision computes an actorType for the authority-ledger row where only a real users.id or users.email match counts as human and autonomy:*, inherit:*, system, and unknown actors are recorded as service, preventing automated approvers from being recorded as human decisions.

createApproval optionally notifies operators via Telegram (pushApproval) only after commit and only when TELEGRAM_PUSH_ENABLED=true, debounced by TELEGRAM_PUSH_DELAY_MS (default 15 s) so an approval that a lane rule auto-approves within the window is skipped as already decided; the actual decision still goes through the normal API as the mapped user with approve:task and SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN enforced server-side.

The opt-in LOOP_REVIEWER_APPROVAL_INHERIT=true path (reviewerInheritsRunApproval) lets a read-only checker/security-checker task inherit its loop run's human-approved maker approval only when the task is proven server-side to be a reviewer lease of that same run via worker_leases.execution_task_id and the maker approval is approved, unexpired, and decided by a real human or exactly one of REVIEWER_INHERITABLE_AUTONOMY_APPROVERS; it never inherits for makers, across runs, from an inherit:*/system/auto/other autonomy:* decision, or after the maker approval expired.
